$comment: Single source for the Quickstart page (docs/src/components/QuickstartSelector) and its CI smoke test (scripts/quickstart_smoke.py). A step or code line applies when every dimension named in its `when` matches the selection. `test` tells the smoke test how to run a step; the page ignores it. See scripts/README.md.

unsupported.reason: SystemOne needs a decision model, which runs locally on Ollama, vLLM, SGLang, or llama.cpp, or on TypeSafe's API. Pick **Ollama** or **All of them**.
RAG needs an embedding model, and Anthropic does not serve one. Pick **All of them** to add Ollama's, or **Docker**, which ships a built-in embedding model.
Codex cannot skip certificate checks, so it cannot connect to the self-signed certificate `ogx go` serves by default. Pick **Insecure** or **Docker**.

Codex talks to the Responses API, which `ogx go` only turns on once it finds an embedding model, and Anthropic does not serve one. Pick **All of them** to add Ollama's, or **Docker**, which ships a built-in embedding model.

steps.title: Pull the models
steps.text: Install [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download), then pull a chat model and an embedding model. The embedding model powers the Responses API, vector stores, and file search.
Coding agents send long prompts. Ollama's default context window cuts them off and the agent gets empty answers, so restart Ollama with a larger one:

test.skip: The CI Ollama container already runs with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384.

steps.title: Set your API keys
steps.text: OGX picks up provider keys from the environment.

test.skip: Keys come from the smoke test's own environment.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.text: With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed, start the server. `ogx go` finds the running backends, installs what they need, and starts serving.

The server listens on https with a self-signed certificate and requires an API key. It prints three generated keys when it starts, and they change every time it restarts:

```text
  ✓ Simple authentication enabled
    Here are keys you can use for authentication:
      ogk_...
```
`--insecure` serves plain http and `--no-auth` turns off API keys. Use them only on your own machine.

steps.text: Run the pre-built [starter image](https://hub.docker.com/r/ogxai/distribution-starter). It serves plain http without API keys, and includes a built-in embedding model.

steps.title: Connect your coding agent
steps.text: Install the agent first: [Claude Code](https://claude.com/download), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), or [opencode](https://opencode.ai). `ogx connect` lists the server's models, points the agent at them, and launches it.
`-k` accepts the server's self-signed certificate for this agent session, like `curl -k`.

A 3B model proves the setup works, but it is too small for real coding work. Pull a larger model that supports tool calling, restart `ogx go`, and pick the model with `--model`, for example `uvx ogx connect claude --model ollama/<model>`.
